ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$, the point $E$ is the midpoint of side $AC$, and point $P$ is a moving point on the median $AD$ of $\triangle ABC$. If $AD = 6$, what is the minimum value of $EP+CP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct point F as the symmetric point of E with respect to AD, and connect CF, which intersects AD at point P,\\
since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, and AD is the median to side BC,\\
therefore $AD\perp BC$,\\
thus AD is the perpendicular bisector of BC,\\
since the corresponding point of E with respect to AD is point F,\\
therefore CF is the minimum value of EP+CP.\\
Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, and E is the midpoint of side AC,\\
thus F is the midpoint of AB,\\
therefore CF is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
thus $CF=AD=\boxed{6}$,\\
which means the minimum value of EP+CP is 6.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$, the point $E$ is the midpoint of side $AC$, and point $P$ is a moving point on the median $AD$ of $\triangle ABC$. If $AD = 6$, what is the minimum value of $EP+CP$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct point F as the symmetric point of E with respect to AD, and connect CF, which intersects AD at point P,\\
since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, and AD is the median to side BC,\\
therefore $AD\perp BC$,\\
thus AD is the perpendicular bisector of BC,\\
since the corresponding point of E with respect to AD is point F,\\
therefore CF is the minimum value of EP+CP.\\
Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, and E is the midpoint of side AC,\\
thus F is the midpoint of AB,\\
therefore CF is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
thus $CF=AD=\boxed{6}$,\\
which means the minimum value of EP+CP is 6
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is a horizontal base; a vertical line segment AD is drawn from A to BC, and D is on BC; point P is located on AD; point E is located on side AC; the broken-line path E-P-C is drawn in the figure. The problem statement gives that triangle ABC is an equilateral triangle, E is the midpoint of AC, P moves on the median AD, and AD=6.
Reasoning: According to the reflection shortest path method, because ABC is an equilateral triangle and AD is a median, AD is also the height and the axis of symmetry. Reflect E about AD to point F, then F is on AB. For any point P on AD, by the reflection property EP=FP, therefore EP+CP=FP+CP. According to the fact that the straight line between two points is shortest or the triangle inequality, when the three points F, P, C are collinear, FP+CP obtains the minimum value, and the minimum value is FC. Also because E is the midpoint of AC, after reflection about the axis of symmetry AD, F is the midpoint of AB, so CF is a median of equilateral triangle ABC. The three medians of an equilateral triangle are equal, therefore CF=AD=6. So the minimum value of EP+CP is 6.
